newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Singapore trader urges EU to scrap coffee duty.
newsitem.headline: Singapore trader urges EU to scrap coffee duty.

text.p: A leading Singaporean coffee trader appealed to the European Union on Friday to scrap a protective 10-percent import duty on processed coffee beans.

Ong Siong Kai, managing director of Hiang Kie Pte Ltd, a Singapore-based commodity trader which traded roughly 40,000 tonnes of green and processed beans last year, said he had asked his government to negotiate with the EU.
"At the moment there is a 10 percent import duty on any processed coffee entering the European market, even decaffeinated green beans," he told Reuters.
"We think it's very protective and unfair. It's a very bad protectionist duty and we can never go into the European market with such an unfair duty imposed on our business," he said.

He, together with other traders based in the island state, had asked the Singaporean government to negotiate with the EU on behalf of the business community "to show that they are interested in trade relations with Europe".
He had met many European companies who were interested in buying his special decaffeinated beans, but as long the 10-percent duty was in place "the price simply is not competitive".
